back: Holstein-Friesian (most milk, lower butterfat), Jersey (richest milk, small, heat tolerant), Guernsey (golden milk), Ayrshire (hardy).
Wedge-shaped, lean and angular; deep body, thin neck, large well-attached udder, prominent milk veins.
Regular times; calm; wash and dry teats; strip cup; milk fully and fast; teat dip; record; filter and cool to about 4 °C; clean utensils.
Inflammation of the udder, usually bacterial: hot swollen quarter, clots, watery or bloody milk; subclinical needs a test.
Hygiene, teat dipping, strip cup, good machines, milk infected cows last, dry-cow therapy, cull chronic cases.
Six to eight weeks before calving: udder renewal, foetal growth, body reserves; steam up in the last weeks.
Yield rises to a peak about 6-8 weeks after calving, then falls slowly; standard lactation 305 days.

front: Why discard milk from treated cows?
back: Antibiotic residues are a health risk and spoil milk for processing; discard for the whole withdrawal period.
